nodes.label: Four-Level SODA Fallback Query Strategy
nodes.rationale: NYC's SODA sign dataset has inconsistent street-name formatting and mid-block coverage gaps, so retrieve_signs() escalates through an exact match (L1), abbreviation-variant retry (L2), broad on-street query with client-side cross-street filtering (L3), and finally a BFS traversal of the street adjacency graph (L4) to cover mid-span blocks that don't align with SODA's own record boundaries.

nodes.label: Index Release Decoupled from Code Release Cadence
nodes.rationale: NYC curb geometry changes independently of code, so the spatial index is rebuilt and republished on a monthly cron to the rolling index-v1 GitHub release via index-rebuild.yml, deliberately kept separate from release.yml's v* code-release cadence; there is no push trigger because the citywide build is too heavy to run per-commit.

nodes.label: Vendored Mirror Sync Pattern
nodes.rationale: HACS-distributed integrations must ship dependencies in-tree, so src/gps2asp/ is mirrored into custom_components/asp_parking/gps2asp/ via scripts/sync_vendored.py; vendor-guard.yml enforces the mirror stays in sync via a dry-run check on every push/PR.

nodes.label: CalDAV Version Compatibility Shim
nodes.rationale: Home Assistant's built-in CalDAV component hard-pins caldav==2.1.0, which takes precedence over the integration's own requirement, while local dev/tests use caldav[async]==3.2.0; _CompatAsyncDAVClient wraps the sync caldav.DAVClient in run_in_executor under 2.1.0 so blocking I/O never hits the HA event loop under either version.
